notes:
Thirty-eight bullets, three independent beastman strongholds, and a mini-quest nested inside the first of them. Bullets 1, 2, 4 and 22 are advice, a key-item checklist, a remark about the ??? spots and a strategy suggestion -- none is a step. Bullets 5, 6, 25, 26-30, 32 and 33 are pure routing and live in the note of the step they lead to. The three-row wikitable after bullet 3 is the quest's real shopping list (Monastic Cavern J-6 / Orcish crest, Qulun Dome J-7 / Quadav crest, Castle Oztroja H-6 / Yagudo crest) and is structure, not steps.

The '== Obtaining the Crimson Orb ==' section IS part of the walkthrough -- its bullets are numbered continuously with everything else, not restarted -- and it is the only way past the Wall of Banishing, so it is laddered in full. It also carries the best evidence on the page: the orb is a single key item that darkens through White > Pink > Red > Blood > Cursed and is finally exchanged for the Crimson orb, and every colour is a separate resource id, so three rungs land on it. The four ponds collapse to ONE step: the page never names them ('touch the ponds at (L-9) -> (I-6) -> (E-8) -> (H-10)'), it says outright they may be touched in any order, and nothing between them is markable -- the marker sits on Sedal-Godjal for the whole detour whether this is one rung or four. Only the Cursed orb is used as evidence there; rungs for Pink, Red and Blood would be rungs the marker provably cannot move between.

The three crests are independent and may be collected in any order. They are deliberately NOT one group -- each branch is internally ordered, and a group is an unordered SET of steps, not of branches. The cost is real and worth writing down: a player who takes the Yagudo crest first jumps the high-water mark straight to Maat with two crests still missing. The turn-in therefore carries all three crests as its requirement list, so it reads grey rather than a yellow '?' until the quest is genuinely finished.

The page contradicts itself about the Quadav crest. The summary table puts it at Qulun Dome (J-7); bullet 19 puts the ??? 'along the west wall in the northern part of (I-7)'. Both are recorded and (I-7) is used, because bullet 19 is the one giving the instruction. The quest is demoted to medium for that, and for the Magicite key-item gate, which is unmodellable in two separate ways at once (it is a mission prerequisite, and the page says a PARTY MEMBER's copy counts).

Ruby Quadav and the two Yagudo High Priests are notes, not mobs. The page says to run past one and to wait out or Trust-tank the other, so recording either as a kill would put a sword marker on something the page explicitly tells you not to fight. The Brass Statue's password list is transcluded from the 'Brass Statue' page and is not in this cache, so the passwords themselves are unrecoverable here.

ADVERSARY PASS. Every other rung survived. Checked: each evidence key item is granted by the bullet its step is built from (White orb b10, Cursed orb b11, Crimson orb b12, Orcish crest b8/14, Quadav crest b20, Yagudo crest b36 via the summary table and the section note) and none of them is the header Reward, which is the level 65 cap and correctly carries no evidence at step 17; no key item is evidence twice; n is dense 1..17; no empty all-list; every NPC, object, monster, item and zone name written here appears in the page text and resolves. The reordering that puts the Crimson orb mini-quest ahead of the Monastic Cavern ??? is the page's own order, not an invention: bullets 13 and 14 restate bullets 7 and 8 after the orb, which is why those pairs are merged. Ruby Quadav and the two Yagudo High Priests are correctly bystanders and not mobs. Step 9 was downgraded for zone conflation, see its note. Two soft spots left standing and named here rather than cut, because the page supports them and only 'medium' is honest about them: the Yagudo torch on step 14 is a section-wide precondition the page never spends anywhere, so pinning it to the torch-lighting is a guess that lets steps 12 and 13 read ready without it; and the ladder has no travel rung into Castle Oztroja or Davoi while it has one into Qulun Dome, which is inconsistent but not something this stage may fix by adding.

Moved out of the player-facing step notes (build vocabulary; see AUTHORING.md, 'Two notes, two audiences'):
  step 7: A partner's Crimson orb drops the wall for everyone in the area, which is the alternative items_partial stands for; the page warns it is not a Tractor shortcut.
  step 9: Kept rather than cut because it is the sole record of the crossing, but it is not a clean one-step-one-zone rung.
  step 10: the page calls it only 'the door to the right after zoning' and never names it, so there is no target to record. that is the alternative items_partial stands for.
  step 14: A party member's torch counts, which is what items_partial records.
  step 17: The reward is the level 65 cap, not an item, so there is nothing to record as evidence.

steps.note: on a level 56 job; he asks for the Orcish, Quadav and Yagudo crests. Bullet 1 (pair this with Nation Mission Magicite 4-1) and bullet 2 (the key-item checklist) are advice and requirements, not steps.
just north of the (J-9) Wall of Banishing. Bullets 5-7 are the route: into Monastic Cavern at Davoi (H-11), out again at (I-8), then round to the (J-9) entrance.
the wall to the south; touching it once is what Sedal-Godjal wants before he will hand anything over.
go back to him after touching the wall.

four ponds at (L-9), (I-6), (E-8) and (H-10), in any order. The page calls them only 'the ponds' and never names them, so there is nothing to point at. Each one darkens the orb a stage -- White > Pink > Red > Blood -- and the fourth turns it into the Cursed orb and inflicts Curse, which Holy Water or Cursna removes. Only the Cursed orb is recorded as evidence: it is the one that proves all four are done.
he swaps the Cursed orb for the Crimson orb. The pond step is wedged between two conversations with the same NPC because the page really does send you away and back.
The same (J-9) wall as step 3, now opened with the orb. Orcs around the wall aggro the moment invisible drops and will interrupt the prompt.
stick to the west wall to stay off the true-sight NMs. The crest sits among cave-flower stalks before the cliff -- do not fall down it. The summary table agrees on (J-6).

In from Beadeaux: tunnel at (H-7) 'A' to map 2, get muted by The Mute at (G-7) so The Afflictor at (G-8) cannot curse you, back to map 1 at (F-8) 'B', ramp to the second level at (E-10), through (I-9) to (K-6), then the path to (M-8) and the Dome. Silent Oil rather than a Sneak spell, because The Mute silences you for about ten minutes. Grid deliberately left empty: the (M-8) entrance belongs to Beadeaux, not to this step's zone. ADVERSARY: downgraded. Bullets 15 and 16 are Beadeaux routing end to end and only the last three words are in Qulun Dome, so this rung carries two zones and the draft had to discard its only grid to keep one.
The three Magicite key items open it, and the page says a player assisting you may hold them instead.

GRID CONFLICT: the summary table says Qulun Dome (J-7), bullet 19 says the northern part of (I-7). (I-7) is used because bullet 19 is the instruction. Along the west wall; hug the south wall past several true-sound NMs and do not drop off the ledge. Ruby Quadav guards the first room -- the page says run past it or zone rather than fight it, so it is not recorded as a monster.

floor 1. Password #1 is in the room at (H-9) near the entrance. Pull one of the levers and run back -- a 50% chance of a trapdoor, and the other handle works once the floor rises again. Stairs at (J-8) lead to map 2. The passwords reset at Vana'diel day change, so time the climb.

floor 2, a different Brass Door from step 12. Password #2: right at the first intersection, west to (G-7) for map 6, north to map 7, password at (H-9). Password #3: back to that intersection, south to the fork at (H-10), left, then the room in the northwest corner of (I-8). The correct lever combination is written behind the hidden door in the east wall at (I-10). Onward at (G-9) to map 3, then the one-way path up the stairs at (H-11) to floor 4; do not run through the leech pool.

Floor 4, the third Brass Door. Light any one of the torches in the corner rooms at (G-7), (G-8), (H-7) or (H-8) and get to the door before it shuts; Reraise if you are low level, and a Thief can Hide off the Yagudo. The page puts the Yagudo torch requirement at the head of the section without saying where it is spent, and this torch-lighting is the only place on the page it could be hence medium.

the pedestal on floor 4. Enter the three passwords, in any order, with proper capitalisation; a wrong guess is reported at once and throws you back to the top of the menu. Bullet 22 says brute-forcing is often quicker than collecting them. The candidate list is transcluded from the 'Brass Statue' page and is NOT in this cache. Release Trusts first or they may not fall through the floor with you. No grid: the page never gives the statue one.

the right password drops you into the courtyard; the spot is on the first platform. The grid is the section note's own 'fourth floor of Castle Oztroja at H-6'. Two true-sight Yagudo High Priests stand here and one usually stands on the spot -- the page says wait it out or let a Trust hold it and Warp after clicking, so neither is recorded as a monster to kill.

All three crests at once. All three are listed here on purpose: the crests may be collected in any order, so the mark can arrive early, and this requirement list keeps it grey until they really are all held.

notes:
Twenty-five bullets covering a whole Ergon weapon, of which only the first ten are the quest the game tracks. Bullet 10 says so outright: after Part 1 the quest moves to the completed log. Packet 0x056 will therefore report this quest DONE from step 9 onwards, and core/steps only gives a position to quests in progress -- so Parts 2 to 4 are laddered honestly here but can never actually carry a marker. Recording them costs nothing and is what the page tells a player to do; hiding them would be the pipeline deciding the page is wrong when it is the game that is odd.

The Nodal Wand is the one thing that cannot be modelled. The wiki writes 'Nodal Wand I / II / III' and none of those resolves; res/items.lua holds THREE items named plainly 'Nodal Wand' (21067, 21068, 21069) with byte-identical names, so no name can ever say which stage you are holding. The bare 'Nodal Wand' -- which the page does use, in the Dropped Item section -- is put on the six trade steps that need the wand in hand, because it is the only form that resolves and a wrong requirement only costs a step its yellow '?', never its marker. items_partial is set on every one of them. It is deliberately NEVER used as evidence: the same resolved id on two steps trips the duplicate gate and demotes the quest outright, and on any one step it would bind two stages out of three to the wrong rung. The five key items carry the ladder instead -- Rusted handbell, Emblazoned handbell, and the Ripple Prominence, Inferno and Cyclone concretions -- five clean evidence points across eighteen steps.

Idris is the header's Reward, so the last step has no evidence at all. The battlefield entry is read as needing the Emblazoned handbell in hand: the page never names the key item it consumes, saying only that 'No key item is consumed if you lose', and the handbell is both what you were just given and what Nhili has to talk about before the water will open. That step is medium for it. Main job GEO is required for that ONE battlefield -- bullet 1 says the quest may be started on any job and bullet 18 says even the third upgrade does not need GEO -- so `jobs` stays empty rather than pinning the whole quest to Geomancer for ever.

The material counts are the page's totals and the page says they go in cumulatively, so a requirement list wanting 200 Ghastly Stones at once reads grey for a player who is halfway; the counts are still recorded, because they are what the step needs. They cross-check against the header: 100 + 500 + 2,500 + 9,999 is the header's H-P Bayld x13,099. 'All Coalitions Legend Rank or higher' has no slot in the schema and no observable predicate, so it gates nothing here. The '== Dropped Item ==' section (bullets 23-25) is a recovery procedure for a mistake rather than a step, and the page marks its own gil figure unverified; the page as a whole is tagged unverified and Information Needed, which is the other half of the medium.

ADVERSARY PASS. No change. Attacked and failed to break: the five key items are each granted by the bullet their step is built from (Rusted handbell b2, Emblazoned handbell b6, Ripple Prominence b13, Inferno b17, Cyclone b21), none repeats, and Idris -- the header Reward -- is correctly absent from step 18, which is exactly where a reward would have been mistaken for evidence. Order is the page's order, bullet 1 through bullet 22, unbroken. Targets are all entities you act on, and the page's bystanders stayed out: Ornery Dhole and Ujlei Zelekko are where you buy the alternatives, not where the step happens, and neither is recorded. Three Ergon Locus rungs sit in three different zones and each carries its own. n is dense 1..18, no empty all-list, every name resolves including the bare 'Nodal Wand', which the page does use in the Dropped Item section. The Emblazoned handbell on step 7 is the one inference and it is page-internal -- 'No key item is consumed if you lose' presupposes one is consumed on a win, and it is the only key item in hand -- so it stays at medium rather than being cut. Parts 2 to 4 are honestly unreachable by any marker, which the draft already says outright; that is a property of the game, not an error in the reading.

Moved out of the player-facing step notes (build vocabulary; see AUTHORING.md, 'Two notes, two audiences'):
  step 10: The page says 'Nodal Wand I'; only the bare 'Nodal Wand' resolves, and it binds one of three identically named ids, which is what items_partial records here and on every later wand trade.

steps.note: she sends you to Dho Gates after the 'forces of darkness'. Any job may start this even though Idris is Geomancer-only. If you are part-way through an Epeolatry you must finish or quit it first; quitting loses the deposited materials but keeps the Broken rapier hilt key item and it can be restarted at once.
map 1. Apex mobs stand round it and aggro by sound. Waypoint #4 Foret de Hennetiel, or a Home Point, sits near the Dho Gates entrance.

Geosuke is the Leafkin at (J-10). The 100 may go in cumulatively, so this count is the total the step needs and not a single trade -- a half-finished player will read grey. Bullet 6 is the outcome of this trade, which is why the key item is this step's evidence and not a step of its own.
you may have to talk twice, or until she talks about the bell.

main job GEO for this one step only. The page never names the key item the battlefield takes, saying only that none is consumed on a loss, so the Emblazoned handbell is read as the entry ticket -- hence medium. Foret de Hennetiel Home Point is close to the Dho Gates entrance.

one on one, no subjob, no Trusts, 15 minutes; re-enterable immediately and the key item survives a loss. She is immune until her luopans are destroyed -- 25 of them, 4% each, leaving her at 1%. Luopans resist everything but darkness and the element their own is weak to, so a staff and Cataclysm clears most of a set at once. The zone is recorded as Dho Gates because that is where the page puts the entrance; it never names the battlefield.

she hands over the base weapon, which the page calls 'Nodal Wand I'. THIS is where the game calls the quest finished -- bullet 10 -- so 0x056 goes to done here and nothing below can be marked. No evidence: all three stages of the wand share the in-game name 'Nodal Wand' across three separate item ids.
Starts Part 2.

totals, traded cumulatively. Ghastly Stone +1 and +2 are refused; trade those to Ornery Dhole for Obsidian Fragments and buy NQ stones back at 50 fragments each, or turn in a Copper Voucher. Runje's 'View materials. (GEO)' option reports progress. Bullet 13 is the outcome, so the concretion is this step's evidence.

upgrades to the page's 'Nodal Wand II' (-2% luopan damage). Marjami Ravine Frontier Station waypoint is nearest the right entrance; two cliffs on the way need the Climbing key item, or wipe and be raised up. The upgraded wand is not evidence -- same three-ids-one-name problem.
starts Part 3.
totals again. Verdigris +1/+2 are refused; NQ costs 100 Obsidian Fragments each from Ornery Dhole.

a different Ergon Locus from step 12 -- only the zone separates them. Gives the page's 'Nodal Wand III' (Magic Accuracy +5, Magic Atk. Bonus +5, -3% luopan damage). You need not be GEO main for this trade. Yahse Hunting Grounds Waypoint #1 then (H-5) is closest; one cliff needs Climbing.
starts Part 4.
the last material turn-in. Wailing +1/+2 are refused; NQ costs 200 Obsidian Fragments each.

the third Ergon Locus, and the end: it hands over Idris. Idris is the header's Reward, so it proves the quest over rather than this step done and is deliberately not recorded as evidence. The Watercrafting key item reaches it, or wipe and be raised across the water; Foret de Hennetiel Frontier Station is the nearest waypoint. Bullets 23-25, the dropped-wand recovery through Geosuke and Runje for a gil fee the page itself marks unverified, are not steps.
